core_obligations: Recall that $R^if_*\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent by the general quasi-coherence statement, so it is the sheaf associated to its module of global sections (proof lines 4019-4024).

Identify those global sections with $H^i(X, \mathcal{F})$ using the Leray identification and the vanishing of higher cohomology of quasi-coherent modules on the affine scheme $\Spec(A)$ (proof lines 4025-4029).
Use the affine criterion for coherence to translate coherence of $R^if_*\mathcal{F}$ into finite generation of $H^i(X, \mathcal{F})$ over $A$ (proof lines 4030-4032).
Apply the coherence of higher direct images under the proper morphism $f$ to conclude that $H^i(X, \mathcal{F})$ is a finite $A$-module for all $i \geq 0$ (proof lines 4032-4033).
proof_roadmap: $R^if_*\mathcal{F}$ as the sheaf associated to its global sections (proof lines 4019-4024).
Identification of the global sections with $H^i(X, \mathcal{F})$ (proof lines 4025-4029).
Coherence as finite generation over the affine base (proof lines 4030-4032).
Conclusion from the coherence of higher direct images (proof lines 4032-4033).
difficulty_reason: The lemma, stated for a Noetherian base and a proper morphism of algebraic spaces, concludes that the cohomology of a coherent module is a finite module over the base ring in every degree (statement lines 4011-4017). The proof is an assembly of three identifications: quasi-coherence of the higher direct images lets them be read off from their global sections, the Leray identification together with vanishing on the affine base computes those global sections as $H^i(X, \mathcal{F})$, and the affine criterion for coherence turns coherence into finite generation. The translation between coherence on the base and finiteness of the cohomology modules is the substance, so the claim is H2.
